text.p: Hundreds of demonstrators gathered near the Belarussian parliament on Saturday to protest at President Alexander Lukashenko's bid to assume greater powers.

Dozens of deputies spent the night inside the chamber, fearing Lukashenko's security services would evict them from parliament just as they had evicted the country's top electoral official, Viktor Gonchar, on Friday.
Police kept a watchful eye on the demonstrators, who shouted "Impeachment!" and cheered the deputies, who were free to move in and out of the chamber.
Parliamentary speaker Semyon Sharetsky told Reuters that occupying the chamber was a necessary step and that the deputies would stay on.
Deputies say they will begin impeachment proceedings against Lukashenko, though he has ignored rulings by rival institutions in the past.

Gonchar, sacked by Lukashenko on Thursday after he vowed not to validate the results of a referendum on November 24 in which Lukashenko is trying to win much broader powers, was again barred by police from entering his office on Saturday.
Echoing parliament and the constitutional court, he has accused the president of breaking the law and called his commission to meet later today at the parliament.

Lukashenko is seeking authority to extend his term by more than two years, to appoint half the electoral commission and constitutional court and to create an upper house of parliament partly appointed by him.
The constitutional court ruled that the November referendum should be advisory and not carry any legal force, but Lukashenko dismissed the ruling by decree, insisting it should be binding.
His opponents in the former Soviet republic, which is sandwiched between Russia and Poland, say Lukashenko is creating a dictatorship.
Western officials and human rights organisations have also expressed concern at Lukashenko's moves.
